title: Measurement error models for remeasured tree heights
content:
Abstract
Tree height growth is a core variable in forest resource analysis and can have outsized impacts on estimates of forest productivity, carbon sequestration rates, and changes to timber supply. On permanent plots, height growth observations contain measurement error from both initial and subsequent measurements. We developed measurement error models in this context for Douglas-fir (Pseudotsuga menziesii) trees in the Pacific Northwest, United States. The standard deviation of an initial height measurement was estimated using a quality assurance dataset from a national forest inventory. We evaluated alternative error models that account for subjective behavior when prior measurements are known. Our objectives were to (i) assess whether systematic remeasurement error exists and (ii) quantify its impacts on growth predictions compared to an independent remeasurement model. The best-fitting model accounted for partial suppression of negative growth measurements and a preference for the initial height measurement, but growth predictions were highly similar to the independent model. Differences were largest for large trees (between 0.28 and 0.40 m/decade). While our results provide moderate evidence that knowledge of initial height measurements obscures growth signals, the magnitude of this effect appears small. These models provide important contributions to forest inventories by clarifying the role of subjective behavior during field staff trainings and by augmenting automated quality assurance processes.
